Any insight appreciated

posts.topic_title: Why would a reflection hologram show a magnified image?
posts.author: Hans
posts.post_subject: Why would a reflection hologram show a magnified image?
posts.content_md:
The magnification of a reflection hologram has all to do with the reference beam and the light that is used to view the hologram.

You could divide into three cases:

1] Reference beam divergence angle = View beam divergence angle: The hologram will re-play in the same size.

2] Reference beam divergence angle < View beam divergence angle: The hologram shows objects bigger.

3] Reference beam divergence angle > View beam divergence angle: The hologram shows objects smaller.

4] (Special case) Reference beam and view beam are parallel: Hologram re-plays at the same size. Using a parallel beam is the preferred method for recording and copying H1 holograms that need to be flipped to make objects appear in front of the hologram.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Why would a reflection hologram show a magnified image?
posts.content_md: A fun thing to play with when you have a replay geometry that is different than the recording geometry is to move the hologram and watch the image swing. This is an anoying abberation. Kaveh has great descriptions of it in his thesis. (Search the wiki for Kaveh thesis to find a link). Kaveh has also made some great animations using ray tracing software to demonstrate this effect.

posts.content_md:
> **Incoherent:** Here's my rig: 15mw DPSS module@532nm (CLM-15 module from Laserglow) - now I sure wish I knew for sure what kinda power that mother is puttin out - there is a sticker on the module stating that some cat tested it for ten minutes at 32mw....?

I'd be very surprised if this laser is suitable for holography. Most of the modules like that end up running multimode or have very short CL.

> **Incoherent:** I have a split-beam arrangement ... and essentially expose the plate from opposite sides...

What sort of subject are you using? How far from the plate is the reference beam expander (lens)?

> **Incoherent:** But for gods' sake I just can't seem to produce a decent hologram, and would LOVE to find out why my latest attempt is a hugely magnified image that seems to cover the entire plate.

Is the magnification different from your previous attempts? Is there a chance that you're at the real image rather than the virtual image? Does the image appear to be turned inside out?

posts.author: dave battin
posts.post_subject: Why would a reflection hologram show a magnified image?
posts.content_md: Did you bleach the hologram? try to flip the hologram over and see if their is an faint image on the opposite side. If you cant see an image when you flip it over, and you cant bleach it out, then I would suggest you make sure the emulsion is facing the laser and not the object.............
